g.text: The maker's five bicolour LEDs (D1-D5 = his LED1-LED5) keep his wiring: every blue anode on one pin, every red anode on another, one resistor each. Blue: D3 through 330 ohm (about 1.5 mA each). Red: D10 through 1.3 k (about 1.1 mA each). His were 22 ohm on an ATtiny85.

g.desc: The maker's five bicolour LEDs (D1-D5 = his LED1-LED5) keep his wiring: every blue anode on one pin, every red anode on another, one resistor each. Blue: D3 through 330 ohm (about 1.5 mA each). Red: D10 through 1.3 k (about 1.1 mA each). His were 22 ohm on an ATtiny85.

g.text: Power: the switch common is the 3.3 V rail (XIAO 3V3 pin). Position 1 = badge 3.3 V feeds the rail. Position 2 (OFF) ties D1 to the rail through R1; position 3 (USB-BAT) leaves the badge disconnected.

g.desc: Power: the switch common is the 3.3 V rail (XIAO 3V3 pin). Position 1 = badge 3.3 V feeds the rail. Position 2 (OFF) ties D1 to the rail through R1; position 3 (USB-BAT) leaves the badge disconnected.

g.text: On USB-BAT the XIAO powers itself from USB-C or the LiPo on J2 (which it charges). Do not plug in USB with the switch on SAO while on a badge: two 3.3 V regulators would share one rail.

g.desc: On USB-BAT the XIAO powers itself from USB-C or the LiPo on J2 (which it charges). Do not plug in USB with the switch on SAO while on a badge: two 3.3 V regulators would share one rail.

g.text: R2, R3: 330 ohm on the SAO GPIO pins per docs/standard.md. R1: 330 ohm in the OFF sense line. No I2C pull-ups on the add-on (the maker had 10 k; the badge provides them).

g.desc: R2, R3: 330 ohm on the SAO GPIO pins per docs/standard.md. R1: 330 ohm in the OFF sense line. No I2C pull-ups on the add-on (the maker had 10 k; the badge provides them).

g.text: Dropped from the maker's circuit: ATtiny85, its 10 k reset pull-up, the two 10 k I2C pull-ups, two 0 ohm links and the six ISP pogo pads. Mode button = the XIAO's BOOT button.
